cards.name: Tangela
cards.flavorText: Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon's true appearance remains a mystery.

cards.name: Tangrowth
cards.flavorText: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.

cards.name: Pinsir
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

cards.name: Spinarak
cards.flavorText: Some fishers weave its sturdy thread into nets to catch fish Pokémon.

cards.name: Ariados
cards.flavorText: It wanders in search of food after darkness falls, never nesting in a specific place.

cards.name: Sunkern
cards.flavorText: It is very weak. Its only means of defense is to shake its leaves desperately at its attacker.

cards.name: Sunflora
cards.flavorText: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.

cards.name: Heracross
cards.flavorText: With its herculean powers, it can easily throw around an object that is 100 times its own weight.

cards.name: Volbeat
cards.flavorText: It flashes the light on its rear to communicate with other Volbeat. It loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.

cards.name: Illumise
cards.flavorText: It guides Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. There are scholars who research the meaning of these signs.

cards.name: Leafeon
cards.flavorText: The younger they are, the more they smell like fresh grass. With age, their fragrance takes on the odor of fallen leaves.

cards.name: Phantump
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon came to be when the spirit of a deceased child possessed a tree stump. It now wanders the forest searching for friends.

cards.name: Trevenant
cards.flavorText: Trevenant is very kind to Pokémon living in the forest. It doesn't even care if these Pokémon take up residence in the greenery on its head.

cards.name: Grookey
cards.flavorText: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.

cards.name: Thwackey
cards.flavorText: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.

cards.name: Rillaboom
cards.flavorText: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.

cards.name: Applin
cards.flavorText: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.flavorText: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

cards.name: Iron Leaves
cards.flavorText: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

cards.name: Poltchageist
cards.flavorText: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

cards.name: Poltchageist
cards.flavorText: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

cards.name: Sinistcha
cards.flavorText: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

cards.name: Teal Mask Ogerpon
cards.flavorText: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

ability.name: Teal Dance
ability.text: Once during your turn, you may attach a Basic Grass Energy card from your hand to this Pokémon. If you attached Energy to a Pokémon in this way, draw a card.

cards.name: Vulpix
cards.flavorText: As its body grows larger, its six warm tails become more beautiful, with a more luxurious coat of fur.

cards.name: Ninetales
cards.flavorText: It has nine long tails and fur that gleams gold. It is said to live for 1,000 years.

cards.name: Slugma
cards.flavorText: It's said that in ancient times, when volcanoes were more active, there were many more Slugma than there are now.

cards.name: Torkoal
cards.flavorText: Coal is the source of Torkoal's energy. Large amounts of coal can be found in the mountains where they live.

cards.name: Chimchar
cards.flavorText: Its fiery rear end is fueled by gas made in its belly. Even rain can't extinguish the fire.

cards.name: Monferno
cards.flavorText: It skillfully controls the intensity of the fire on its tail to keep its foes at an ideal distance.

cards.name: Infernape
cards.flavorText: Its crown of fire is indicative of its fiery nature. It is beaten by none in terms of quickness.

cards.name: Darumaka
cards.flavorText: It derives its power from fire burning inside its body. If the fire dwindles, this Pokémon will immediately fall asleep.

cards.name: Darmanitan
cards.flavorText: The thick arms of this hot-blooded Pokémon can deliver punches capable of obliterating a dump truck.

cards.name: Litwick
cards.flavorText: While shining a light and pretending to be a guide, it leeches off the life-force of any who follow it.

cards.name: Lampent
cards.flavorText: The spirits it absorbs fuel its baleful fire. It hangs around hospitals waiting for people to pass on.

cards.name: Chandelure
cards.flavorText: It absorbs spirits, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

cards.name: Chi-Yu
cards.flavorText: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

cards.name: Poliwag
cards.flavorText: Its legs are newly grown, and it can't walk very well. It seems to prefer swimming through the water instead.

cards.name: Poliwhirl
cards.flavorText: Its skin is moist all over its body. The skin on its belly spiral also feels smooth.

cards.name: Poliwrath
cards.flavorText: It can use its well-developed arms and legs to run on the surface of the water for a split second.

cards.name: Goldeen
cards.flavorText: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.

cards.name: Seaking
cards.flavorText: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.

cards.name: Jynx
cards.flavorText: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.

cards.name: Corphish
cards.flavorText: It can live in impure water, where it doesn't need to compete with other water Pokémon for food, so its numbers have steadily increased.

cards.name: Crawdaunt
cards.flavorText: A rough customer that wildly flails its giant claws. It is said to be extremely hard to raise.

cards.name: Feebas
cards.flavorText: It is the shabbiest Pokémon of all. It forms schools and lives at the bottom of rivers that teem with plant life.

cards.name: Milotic
cards.flavorText: It lives at the bottom of clear lakes. In times of war, it shows itself, which soothes people's minds and hearts.

cards.name: Snorunt
cards.flavorText: It is said that a home visited by a Snorunt will prosper. It can withstand cold of −150 degrees Fahrenheit.

cards.name: Glalie
cards.flavorText: It prevents prey from escaping by instantaneously freezing moisture in the air.

cards.name: Froslass
cards.flavorText: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

cards.name: Glaceon
cards.flavorText: It lowers its body heat to freeze its fur. The hairs then become like needles it can fire.

cards.name: Phione
cards.flavorText: When the water warms, they inflate the flotation sac on their heads and drift languidly on the sea in packs.

cards.name: Froakie
cards.flavorText: It secretes flexible bubbles from its chest and back. The bubbles reduce the damage it would otherwise take when attacked.

cards.name: Frogadier
cards.flavorText: It can throw bubble-covered pebbles with precise control, hitting empty cans up to a hundred feet away.

cards.name: Cramorant
cards.flavorText: It's an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

cards.name: Finizen
cards.flavorText: Its water ring is made from seawater mixed with a sticky fluid that Finizen secretes from its blowhole.

cards.name: Palafin
cards.flavorText: Its physical capabilities are no different than a Finizen's, but when its allies are in danger, it transforms and powers itself up.

ability.name: Hero's Spirit
ability.text: Put this Pokémon into play only with the effect of Palafin's Zero to Hero Ability.

cards.name: Iron Bundle
cards.flavorText: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

cards.name: Walking Wake
cards.flavorText: This ferocious creature is shrouded in mystery. It's named after an aquatic monster mentioned in an old expedition journal.

cards.name: Zapdos
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon has complete control over electricity. There are tales of Zapdos nesting in the dark depths of pitch-black thunderclouds.

cards.name: Shinx
cards.flavorText: The extension and contraction of its muscles generates electricity. Its fur glows when it's in trouble.

cards.name: Luxio
cards.flavorText: By gathering their tails together, they collectively generate powerful electricity from their claws.

cards.name: Emolga
cards.flavorText: As Emolga flutters through the air, it crackles with electricity. This Pokémon is cute, but it can cause a lot of trouble.

cards.name: Helioptile
cards.flavorText: When spread, the frills on its head act like solar panels, generating the power behind this Pokémon's electric moves.

cards.name: Heliolisk
cards.flavorText: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.

cards.name: Morpeko
cards.flavorText: It has a small stomach. If it isn't constantly eating the seeds it keeps in its pockets, it will get hungry immediately.

cards.name: Tadbulb
cards.flavorText: It floats using the electricity stored in its body. When thunderclouds are around, Tadbulb will float higher off the ground.

cards.name: Bellibolt
cards.flavorText: What appear to be eyeballs are actually organs for discharging the electricity generated by Bellibolt's belly-button dynamo.

cards.name: Wattrel
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they're a popular delicacy.

cards.name: Kilowattrel
cards.flavorText: It uses its throat sac to store electricity generated by its wings. There's hardly any oil in its feathers, so it is a poor swimmer.

ability.name: Initialization
ability.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, Pokémon with a Rule Box in play (both yours and your opponent's) have no Abilities, except for Future Pokémon. (Pokémon ex, Pokémon V, etc. have Rule Boxes.)

cards.name: Clefairy
cards.flavorText: On nights with a full moon, they gather together and dance. The surrounding area is enveloped in an abnormal magnetic field.

cards.name: Clefable
cards.flavorText: It has an acute sense of hearing. It can easily hear a pin being dropped nearly 1,100 yards away.

cards.name: Abra
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon uses its psychic powers while it sleeps. The contents of Abra's dreams affect the powers that the Pokémon wields.

cards.name: Kadabra
cards.flavorText: Using its psychic power, Kadabra levitates as it sleeps. It uses its springy tail as a pillow.

cards.name: Alakazam
cards.flavorText: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.

cards.name: Girafarig
cards.flavorText: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

cards.name: Farigiraf
cards.flavorText: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

cards.name: Chimecho
cards.flavorText: Its cries echo inside its hollow body to emerge as beautiful notes for startling and repelling foes.

cards.name: Flabébé
cards.flavorText: This Flabébé rides a red flower. Immediately after birth, this Pokémon begins flying around in search of a flower it likes.

cards.name: Floette
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon uses red wavelengths of light to pour its own energy into flowers and draw forth their latent potential.

cards.name: Florges
cards.flavorText: They say that flower gardens created by Florges are constantly showered with a power that can heal both body and spirit.

cards.name: Swirlix
cards.flavorText: It eats its own weight in sugar every day. If it doesn't get enough sugar, it becomes incredibly grumpy.

cards.name: Slurpuff
cards.flavorText: By taking in a person's scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It's hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.

cards.name: Sandygast
cards.flavorText: It flings sand into the eyes of its prey and tries to close in on them while they're blinded, but since Sandygast is so slow, the prey tends to escape.

cards.name: Palossand
cards.flavorText: From the hollows in its arms, it fires the bones of its victims, which are all dried up after being drained of their vitality.

cards.name: Enamorus
cards.flavorText: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

cards.name: Munkidori
cards.flavorText: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

cards.name: Fezandipiti
cards.flavorText: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

cards.name: Sandshrew
cards.flavorText: No matter how high a place it falls from, this Pokémon can save itself by rolling into a ball and bouncing.

cards.name: Sandslash
cards.flavorText: The spikes on its body are made up of its hardened hide. It rolls up and attacks foes with its spikes.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe
cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Hisuian Arcanine
cards.flavorText: Snaps at its foes with fangs cloaked in blazing flame. Despite its bulk, it deftly feints every which way, leading opponents on a deceptively merry chase as it all but dances around them.

cards.name: Nosepass
cards.flavorText: When endangered, it may protect itself by increasing its magnetism and drawing nearby iron objects to its body.

cards.name: Probopass
cards.flavorText: Probopass radiates such a powerful magnetic field that nearby electrical appliances are rendered useless while it's around.

cards.name: Timburr
cards.flavorText: It fights by swinging a piece of lumber around. It is close to evolving when it can handle heavy lumber without difficulty.

cards.name: Gurdurr
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

cards.name: Conkeldurr
cards.flavorText: Rather than rely on their strength, they master moves that make good use of centrifugal force to swing around concrete.

cards.name: Hawlucha
cards.flavorText: Hawlucha live quietly without flocking together. They fight constantly with their natural enemies: noisy groups of Primeape.

cards.name: Glimmet
cards.flavorText: Glimmet's toxic mineral crystals look just like flower petals. This Pokémon scatters poisonous powder like pollen to protect itself.

cards.name: Glimmora
cards.flavorText: Glimmora's petals are made of crystallized poison energy. It has recently become evident that these petals resemble Tera Jewels.

cards.name: Ting-Lu
cards.flavorText: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

cards.name: Okidogi
cards.flavorText: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

ability.name: Cornerstone Stance
ability.text: Prevent all damage from attacks done to this Pokémon by your opponent's Pokémon that have an Ability.

cards.name: Poochyena
cards.flavorText: Poochyena pursue their prey in packs. Once the prey is exhausted, the pack finishes it off. But sometimes the prey retaliates, and the pack flees.

cards.name: Mightyena
cards.flavorText: Once it's caught the scent of faraway prey, the leader gives a signal, and the whole pack moves out.

cards.name: Venipede
cards.flavorText: Venipede and Sizzlipede are similar species, but when the two meet, a huge fight ensues.

cards.name: Whirlipede
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon spins itself rapidly and charges into its opponents. Its top speed is just over 60 mph.

cards.name: Scolipede
cards.flavorText: Scolipede latches on to its prey with the claws on its neck before slamming them into the ground and jabbing them with its claws' toxic spikes.

cards.name: Brute Bonnet
cards.flavorText: It is possible that the creature listed as Brute Bonnet in a certain book could actually be this Pokémon.

cards.name: Skarmory
cards.flavorText: People fashion swords from Skarmory's shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.

cards.name: Aron
cards.flavorText: It eats iron ore—and sometimes railroad tracks— to build up the steel armor that protects its body.

cards.name: Lairon
cards.flavorText: Lairon live in mountains brimming with spring water and iron ore, so these Pokémon often came into conflict with humans in the past.

cards.name: Aggron
cards.flavorText: Aggron has a horn sharp enough to perforate thick iron sheets. It brings down its opponents by ramming into them horn first.

cards.name: Heatran
cards.flavorText: It dwells in volcanic caves. It digs in with its cross-shaped feet to crawl on ceilings and walls.

cards.name: Varoom
cards.flavorText: The steel section is Varoom's actual body. This Pokémon clings to rocks and converts the minerals within into energy to fuel its activities.

cards.name: Revavroom
cards.flavorText: Revavroom viciously threatens others with the sound of its exhaust. It sticks its tongue out from its cylindrical mouth and sprays toxic fluids.

cards.name: Applin
cards.flavorText: Applin lives inside an apple. When an Applin is separated from its apple, its body loses moisture and the Pokémon grows weak.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.flavorText: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

cards.name: Dreepy
cards.flavorText: It has a habit of biting at Clauncher even though it doesn't feed on them. This is said to be vestigial behavior from when Dreepy was alive.

cards.name: Drakloak
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon stores up energy in its lungs, then shoots it out. It takes care of Dreepy and battles alongside them until they're all grown up.

cards.name: Tatsugiri
cards.flavorText: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

cards.name: Farfetch'd
cards.flavorText: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. In a dire situation, the stalk can also serve as food.

cards.name: Chansey
cards.flavorText: It walks carefully to prevent its egg from breaking. However, it is extremely fast at running away.

ability.name: Happy Switch
ability.text: Once during your turn, you may move a Basic Energy from 1 of your Pokémon to another of your Pokémon.

cards.name: Eevee
cards.flavorText: Its genetic code is irregular. It may mutate if it is exposed to radiation from element stones.

cards.name: Snorlax
cards.flavorText: Its stomach's digestive juices can dissolve any kind of poison. Eating things off the ground doesn't bother it at all.

cards.name: Aipom
cards.flavorText: Its tail moves with greater dexterity than its hands. Making deft use of this tail, Aipom lives high among the treetops.

cards.name: Ambipom
cards.flavorText: Split into two, the tails are so adept at handling and doing things that Ambipom rarely uses its hands.

cards.name: Ducklett
cards.flavorText: It strengthens its body by diving into the depths of ponds, swimming around while looking for bog moss to eat.

cards.name: Swanna
cards.flavorText: It's said that many artists have taken inspiration from the sight of a Swanna performing a beautiful dance in the light of dawn.

ability.name: Seasoned Skill
ability.text: Blood Moon used by this Pokémon costs Colorless less for each Prize card your opponent has taken.

cards.name: Pinsir
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.

cards.name: Sunflora
cards.flavorText: Since it converts sunlight into energy, it is always looking in the direction of the sun.

cards.name: Dipplin
cards.flavorText: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

cards.name: Poltchageist
cards.flavorText: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

cards.name: Torkoal
cards.flavorText: Coal is the source of Torkoal's energy. Large amounts of coal can be found in the mountains where they live.

cards.name: Infernape
cards.flavorText: Its crown of fire is indicative of its fiery nature. It is beaten by none in terms of quickness.

cards.name: Froslass
cards.flavorText: It freezes prey by blowing its −58 degree Fahrenheit breath. It is said to then secretly display its prey.

cards.name: Phione
cards.flavorText: When the water warms, they inflate the flotation sac on their heads and drift languidly on the sea in packs.

cards.name: Cramorant
cards.flavorText: It's an incredibly poor learner because it uses the bare minimum amount of energy for its brain. It focuses on battling instead.

cards.name: Heliolisk
cards.flavorText: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.

cards.name: Wattrel
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon make their nests on coastal cliffs. The nests have a strange, crackling texture, and they're a popular delicacy.

cards.name: Chimecho
cards.flavorText: Its cries echo inside its hollow body to emerge as beautiful notes for startling and repelling foes.

cards.name: Enamorus
cards.flavorText: When it flies to this land from across the sea, the bitter winter comes to an end. According to legend, this Pokémon's love gives rise to the budding of fresh life across Hisui.

cards.name: Hisuian Growlithe
cards.flavorText: They patrol their territory in pairs. I believe the igneous rock components in the fur of this species are the result of volcanic activity in its habitat.

cards.name: Snivy
cards.flavorText: It is very intelligent and calm. Being exposed to lots of sunlight makes its movements swifter.

cards.name: Servine
cards.flavorText: It moves along the ground as if sliding. Its swift movements befuddle its foes, and it then attacks with a vine whip.

ability.name: Regal Cheer
ability.text: Attacks used by your Pokémon do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Pansage
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon dwells deep in the forest. Eating a leaf from its head whisks weariness away as if by magic.

cards.name: Simisage
cards.flavorText: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

cards.name: Petilil
cards.flavorText: The leaves on its head are very bitter. Eating one of these leaves is known to refresh a tired body.

cards.name: Lilligant
cards.flavorText: Even veteran Trainers face a challenge in getting its beautiful flower to bloom. This Pokémon is popular with celebrities.

cards.name: Maractus
cards.flavorText: It uses an up-tempo song and dance to drive away the bird Pokémon that prey on its flower seeds.

cards.name: Karrablast
cards.flavorText: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.

cards.name: Foongus
cards.flavorText: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.

cards.name: Amoonguss
cards.flavorText: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.

cards.name: Victini
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

cards.name: Darumaka
cards.flavorText: When its internal fire is burning, it cannot calm down and it runs around. When the fire diminishes, it falls asleep.

cards.name: Darmanitan
cards.flavorText: Its internal fire burns at 2,500° F, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.

cards.name: Larvesta
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.

cards.name: Volcarona
cards.flavorText: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona's fire provided a replacement for the sun.

cards.name: Panpour
cards.flavorText: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

cards.name: Simipour
cards.flavorText: The tuft on its head holds water. When the level runs low, it replenishes the tuft by siphoning up water with its tail.

cards.name: Tympole
cards.flavorText: They warn others of danger by vibrating their cheeks to create a high-pitched sound.

cards.name: Palpitoad
cards.flavorText: When they vibrate the bumps on their heads, they can make waves in water or earthquake-like vibrations on land.

cards.name: Seismitoad
cards.flavorText: They shoot paralyzing liquid from their head bumps. They use vibration to hurt their opponents.

cards.name: Tirtouga
cards.flavorText: Restored from a fossil, this Pokémon can dive to depths beyond half a mile.

cards.name: Carracosta
cards.flavorText: They can live both in the ocean and on land. A slap from one of them is enough to open a hole in the bottom of a tanker.

cards.name: Alomomola
cards.flavorText: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.

cards.name: Cubchoo
cards.flavorText: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.

cards.name: Beartic
cards.flavorText: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.

cards.name: Cryogonal
cards.flavorText: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.

cards.name: Emolga
cards.flavorText: The energy made in its cheeks' electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.

cards.name: Tynamo
cards.flavorText: While one alone doesn't have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

cards.name: Eelektrik
cards.flavorText: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.

cards.name: Eelektross
cards.flavorText: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

cards.name: Thundurus
cards.flavorText: Countless charred remains mar the landscape of places through which Thundurus has passed.

cards.name: Munna
cards.flavorText: Munna always float in the air. People whose dreams are eaten by them forget what the dreams had been about.

cards.name: Musharna
cards.flavorText: The mist emanating from their foreheads is packed with the dreams of people and Pokémon.

cards.name: Solosis
cards.flavorText: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.

cards.name: Duosion
cards.flavorText: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.

cards.name: Reuniclus
cards.flavorText: When Reuniclus shake hands, a network forms between their brains, increasing their psychic power.

cards.name: Elgyem
cards.flavorText: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent's brain, causing unendurable headaches.

cards.name: Beheeyem
cards.flavorText: It can manipulate an opponent's memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.

cards.name: Golett
cards.flavorText: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.

cards.name: Golurk
cards.flavorText: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.

ability.name: Debut Performance
ability.text: If you go first, this Pokémon can use attacks during your first turn.

cards.name: Drilbur
cards.flavorText: It can dig through the ground at a speed of 30 mph. It could give a car running aboveground a good race.

cards.name: Timburr
cards.flavorText: It fights by swinging a piece of lumber around. It is close to evolving when it can handle the lumber without difficulty.

cards.name: Gurdurr
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

cards.name: Conkeldurr
cards.flavorText: It is thought that Conkeldurr taught humans how to make concrete more than 2,000 years ago.

cards.name: Throh
cards.flavorText: When it tightens its belt, it becomes stronger. Wild Throh use vines to weave their own belts.

cards.name: Dwebble
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can easily melt holes in hard rocks with a liquid secreted from its mouth.

cards.name: Crustle
cards.flavorText: Competing for territory, Crustle fight viciously. The one whose boulder is broken is the loser of the battle.

cards.name: Landorus
cards.flavorText: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”

cards.name: Venipede
cards.flavorText: Its bite injects a potent poison, enough to paralyze large bird Pokémon that try to prey on it.

cards.name: Whirlipede
cards.flavorText: Protected by a hard shell, it spins its body like a wheel and crashes furiously into its enemies.

cards.name: Scolipede
cards.flavorText: With quick movements, it chases down its foes, attacking relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.

cards.name: Sandile
cards.flavorText: They live buried in the sands of the desert. The sun-warmed sands prevent their body temperature from dropping.

cards.name: Krokorok
cards.flavorText: They live in groups of a few individuals. Protective membranes shield their eyes from sandstorms.

cards.name: Krookodile
cards.flavorText: They never allow prey to escape. Their jaws are so powerful, they can crush the body of an automobile.

cards.name: Escavalier
cards.flavorText: They fly around at high speed, striking with their pointed spears. Even when in trouble, they face opponents bravely.

cards.name: Klink
cards.flavorText: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.

cards.name: Klang
cards.flavorText: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.

cards.name: Klinklang
cards.flavorText: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.

cards.name: Pawniard
cards.flavorText: Blades comprise this Pokémon's entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.

cards.name: Bisharp
cards.flavorText: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.

cards.name: Cobalion
cards.flavorText: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.

ability.name: Metallic Signal
ability.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 2 Evolution Metal Pokémon, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.name: Axew
cards.flavorText: They use their tusks to crush the berries they eat. Repeated regrowth makes their tusks strong and sharp.

cards.name: Fraxure
cards.flavorText: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they've been fighting.

cards.name: Haxorus
cards.flavorText: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.

cards.name: Pidove
cards.flavorText: Each follows its Trainer's orders as best it can, but they sometimes fail to understand complicated commands.

cards.name: Tranquill
cards.flavorText: It can return to its Trainer's location regardless of the distance separating them.

cards.name: Unfezant
cards.flavorText: Males swing their head plumage to threaten opponents. The females' flying abilities surpass those of the males.

cards.name: Audino
cards.flavorText: It touches others with the feelers on its ears, using the sound of their heartbeats to tell how they are feeling.

cards.name: Minccino
cards.flavorText: They greet one another by rubbing each other with their tails, which are always kept well groomed and clean.

cards.name: Cinccino
cards.flavorText: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.

cards.name: Rufflet
cards.flavorText: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.

cards.name: Braviary
cards.flavorText: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.

cards.name: Snivy
cards.flavorText: It is very intelligent and calm. Being exposed to lots of sunlight makes its movements swifter.

cards.name: Servine
cards.flavorText: It moves along the ground as if sliding. Its swift movements befuddle its foes, and it then attacks with a vine whip.

cards.name: Pansage
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon dwells deep in the forest. Eating a leaf from its head whisks weariness away as if by magic.

cards.name: Simisage
cards.flavorText: Ill tempered, it fights by swinging its barbed tail around wildly. The leaf growing on its head is very bitter.

cards.name: Petilil
cards.flavorText: The leaves on its head are very bitter. Eating one of these leaves is known to refresh a tired body.

cards.name: Lilligant
cards.flavorText: Even veteran Trainers face a challenge in getting its beautiful flower to bloom. This Pokémon is popular with celebrities.

cards.name: Maractus
cards.flavorText: It uses an up-tempo song and dance to drive away the bird Pokémon that prey on its flower seeds.

cards.name: Karrablast
cards.flavorText: These mysterious Pokémon evolve when they receive electrical stimulation while they are in the same place as Shelmet.

cards.name: Foongus
cards.flavorText: It lures people in with its Poké Ball pattern, then releases poison spores. Why it resembles a Poké Ball is unknown.

cards.name: Amoonguss
cards.flavorText: It lures prey close by dancing and waving its arm caps, which resemble Poké Balls, in a swaying motion.

cards.name: Darumaka
cards.flavorText: When its internal fire is burning, it cannot calm down and it runs around. When the fire diminishes, it falls asleep.

cards.name: Darmanitan
cards.flavorText: Its internal fire burns at 2,500° F, making enough power that it can destroy a dump truck with one punch.

cards.name: Larvesta
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon was believed to have been born from the sun. When it evolves, its entire body is engulfed in flames.

cards.name: Volcarona
cards.flavorText: When volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere, it is said that Volcarona's fire provided a replacement for the sun.

cards.name: Panpour
cards.flavorText: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

cards.name: Simipour
cards.flavorText: The tuft on its head holds water. When the level runs low, it replenishes the tuft by siphoning up water with its tail.

cards.name: Tympole
cards.flavorText: They warn others of danger by vibrating their cheeks to create a high-pitched sound.

cards.name: Palpitoad
cards.flavorText: When they vibrate the bumps on their heads, they can make waves in water or earthquake-like vibrations on land.

cards.name: Seismitoad
cards.flavorText: They shoot paralyzing liquid from their head bumps. They use vibration to hurt their opponents.

cards.name: Tirtouga
cards.flavorText: Restored from a fossil, this Pokémon can dive to depths beyond half a mile.

cards.name: Carracosta
cards.flavorText: They can live both in the ocean and on land. A slap from one of them is enough to open a hole in the bottom of a tanker.

cards.name: Alomomola
cards.flavorText: The special membrane enveloping Alomomola has the ability to heal wounds.

cards.name: Cubchoo
cards.flavorText: When it is not feeling well, its mucus gets watery and the power of its Ice-type moves decreases.

cards.name: Beartic
cards.flavorText: It can make its breath freeze at will. Very able in the water, it swims around in northern seas and catches prey.

cards.name: Cryogonal
cards.flavorText: When its body temperature goes up, it turns into steam and vanishes. When its temperature lowers, it returns to ice.

cards.name: Emolga
cards.flavorText: The energy made in its cheeks' electric pouches is stored inside its membrane and released while it is gliding.

cards.name: Tynamo
cards.flavorText: While one alone doesn't have much power, a chain of many Tynamo can be as powerful as lightning.

cards.name: Eelektrik
cards.flavorText: They coil around foes and shock them with electricity-generating organs that seem simply to be circular patterns.

cards.name: Eelektross
cards.flavorText: They crawl out of the ocean using their arms. They will attack prey on shore and immediately drag it into the ocean.

cards.name: Munna
cards.flavorText: Munna always float in the air. People whose dreams are eaten by them forget what the dreams had been about.

cards.name: Musharna
cards.flavorText: The mist emanating from their foreheads is packed with the dreams of people and Pokémon.

cards.name: Solosis
cards.flavorText: They drive away attackers by unleashing psychic power. They can use telepathy to talk with others.

cards.name: Duosion
cards.flavorText: Since they have two divided brains, at times they suddenly try to take two different actions at once.

cards.name: Elgyem
cards.flavorText: It uses its strong psychic power to squeeze its opponent's brain, causing unendurable headaches.

cards.name: Beheeyem
cards.flavorText: It can manipulate an opponent's memory. Apparently, it communicates by flashing its three different-colored fingers.

cards.name: Golett
cards.flavorText: The energy that burns inside it enables it to move, but no one has yet been able to identify this energy.

cards.name: Golurk
cards.flavorText: It flies across the sky at Mach speeds. Removing the seal on its chest makes its internal energy go out of control.

cards.name: Drilbur
cards.flavorText: It can dig through the ground at a speed of 30 mph. It could give a car running aboveground a good race.

cards.name: Timburr
cards.flavorText: It fights by swinging a piece of lumber around. It is close to evolving when it can handle the lumber without difficulty.

cards.name: Gurdurr
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon is so muscular and strongly built that even a group of wrestlers could not make it budge an inch.

cards.name: Conkeldurr
cards.flavorText: It is thought that Conkeldurr taught humans how to make concrete more than 2,000 years ago.

cards.name: Throh
cards.flavorText: When it tightens its belt, it becomes stronger. Wild Throh use vines to weave their own belts.

cards.name: Dwebble
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon can easily melt holes in hard rocks with a liquid secreted from its mouth.

cards.name: Crustle
cards.flavorText: Competing for territory, Crustle fight viciously. The one whose boulder is broken is the loser of the battle.

cards.name: Landorus
cards.flavorText: Lands visited by Landorus grant such bountiful crops that it has been hailed as “The Guardian of the Fields.”

cards.name: Venipede
cards.flavorText: Its bite injects a potent poison, enough to paralyze large bird Pokémon that try to prey on it.

cards.name: Whirlipede
cards.flavorText: Protected by a hard shell, it spins its body like a wheel and crashes furiously into its enemies.

cards.name: Scolipede
cards.flavorText: With quick movements, it chases down its foes, attacking relentlessly with its horns until it prevails.

cards.name: Sandile
cards.flavorText: They live buried in the sands of the desert. The sun-warmed sands prevent their body temperature from dropping.

cards.name: Krokorok
cards.flavorText: They live in groups of a few individuals. Protective membranes shield their eyes from sandstorms.

cards.name: Krookodile
cards.flavorText: They never allow prey to escape. Their jaws are so powerful, they can crush the body of an automobile.

cards.name: Escavalier
cards.flavorText: They fly around at high speed, striking with their pointed spears. Even when in trouble, they face opponents bravely.

cards.name: Klink
cards.flavorText: The two minigears that mesh together are predetermined. Each will rebound from other minigears without meshing.

cards.name: Klang
cards.flavorText: By changing the direction in which it rotates, it communicates its feelings to others. When angry, it rotates faster.

cards.name: Klinklang
cards.flavorText: Its red core functions as an energy tank. It fires the charged energy through its spikes into an area.

cards.name: Pawniard
cards.flavorText: Blades comprise this Pokémon's entire body. If battling dulls the blades, it sharpens them on stones by the river.

cards.name: Bisharp
cards.flavorText: It leads a group of Pawniard. It battles to become the boss, but will be driven from the group if it loses.

cards.name: Cobalion
cards.flavorText: This legendary Pokémon battled against humans to protect Pokémon. Its personality is calm and composed.

cards.name: Axew
cards.flavorText: They use their tusks to crush the berries they eat. Repeated regrowth makes their tusks strong and sharp.

cards.name: Fraxure
cards.flavorText: Since a broken tusk will not grow back, they diligently sharpen their tusks on river rocks after they've been fighting.

cards.name: Haxorus
cards.flavorText: They are kind but can be relentless when defending territory. They challenge foes with tusks that can cut steel.

cards.name: Pidove
cards.flavorText: Each follows its Trainer's orders as best it can, but they sometimes fail to understand complicated commands.

cards.name: Tranquill
cards.flavorText: It can return to its Trainer's location regardless of the distance separating them.

cards.name: Unfezant
cards.flavorText: Males swing their head plumage to threaten opponents. The females' flying abilities surpass those of the males.

cards.name: Audino
cards.flavorText: It touches others with the feelers on its ears, using the sound of their heartbeats to tell how they are feeling.

cards.name: Minccino
cards.flavorText: They greet one another by rubbing each other with their tails, which are always kept well groomed and clean.

cards.name: Cinccino
cards.flavorText: Their white fur is coated in a special oil that makes it easy for them to deflect attacks.

cards.name: Rufflet
cards.flavorText: They crush berries with their talons. They bravely stand up to any opponent, no matter how strong it is.

cards.name: Braviary
cards.flavorText: They fight for their friends without any thought about danger to themselves. One can carry a car while flying.

ability.name: Regal Cheer
ability.text: Attacks used by your Pokémon do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

ability.name: Debut Performance
ability.text: If you go first, this Pokémon can use attacks during your first turn.

ability.name: Metallic Signal
ability.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 2 Evolution Metal Pokémon, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

ability.name: Regal Cheer
ability.text: Attacks used by your Pokémon do 20 more damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon (before applying Weakness and Resistance).

ability.name: Debut Performance
ability.text: If you go first, this Pokémon can use attacks during your first turn.

ability.name: Metallic Signal
ability.text: Once during your turn, you may search your deck for up to 2 Evolution Metal Pokémon, reveal them, and put them into your hand. Then, shuffle your deck.

cards.name: Victini
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

cards.name: Sewaddle
cards.flavorText: Leavanny dress it in clothes they made for it when it hatched. It hides its head in its hood while it is sleeping.

cards.name: Swadloon
cards.flavorText: Forests where Swadloon live have superb foliage because the nutrients they make from fallen leaves nourish the plant life.

cards.name: Leavanny
cards.flavorText: Upon finding a small Pokémon, it weaves clothing for it from leaves, using the cutters on its arms and sticky silk.

cards.name: Cottonee
cards.flavorText: When attacked, it escapes by shooting cotton from its body. The cotton serves as a decoy to distract the attacker.

cards.name: Deerling
cards.flavorText: The color and scent of their fur changes to match the mountain grass. When they sense hostility, they hide in the grass.

cards.name: Sawsbuck
cards.flavorText: They migrate according to the seasons. People can tell the season by looking at Sawsbuck's horns.

cards.name: Shelmet
cards.flavorText: When attacked, it defends itself by closing the lid of its shell. It can spit a sticky, poisonous liquid.

cards.name: Accelgor
cards.flavorText: When its body dries out, it weakens. So, to prevent dehydration, it wraps itself in many layers of thin membrane.

cards.name: Virizion
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon fought humans in order to protect its friends. Legends about it continue to be passed down.

cards.name: Tepig
cards.flavorText: It can deftly dodge its foe's attacks while shooting fireballs from its nose. It roasts berries before it eats them.

cards.name: Pignite
cards.flavorText: When its internal fire flares up, its movements grow sharper and faster. When in trouble, it emits smoke.

cards.name: Emboar
cards.flavorText: It can throw a fire punch by setting its fists on fire with its fiery chin. It cares deeply about its friends.

cards.name: Pansear
cards.flavorText: When it is angered, the temperature of its head tuft reaches 600° F. It uses its tuft to roast berries.

cards.name: Simisear
cards.flavorText: It loves sweets because they become energy for the fire burning inside its body.

cards.name: Litwick
cards.flavorText: Litwick shines a light that absorbs the life energy of people and Pokémon, which becomes the fuel that it burns.

cards.name: Lampent
cards.flavorText: This ominous Pokémon is feared. Through cities it wanders, searching for the spirits of the fallen.

cards.name: Chandelure
cards.flavorText: It absorbs a spirit, which it then burns. By waving the flames on its arms, it puts its foes into a hypnotic trance.

cards.name: Heatmor
cards.flavorText: It breathes through a hole in its tail while it burns with an internal fire. Durant is its prey.

cards.name: Oshawott
cards.flavorText: It fights using the scalchop on its stomach. In response to an attack, it retaliates immediately by slashing.

cards.name: Dewott
cards.flavorText: Strict training is how it learns its flowing double-scalchop technique.

cards.name: Samurott
cards.flavorText: One swing of the sword incorporated in its armor can fell an opponent. A simple glare from one of them quiets everybody.

cards.name: Basculin
cards.flavorText: Red and blue Basculin get along so poorly, they'll start fighting instantly. These Pokémon are very hostile.

cards.name: Ducklett
cards.flavorText: These bird Pokémon are excellent divers. They swim around in the water eating their favorite food--peat moss.

cards.name: Swanna
cards.flavorText: Swanna start to dance at dusk. The one dancing in the middle is the leader of the flock.

cards.name: Vanillite
cards.flavorText: The temperature of their breath is -58° F. They create snow crystals and make snow fall in the areas around them.

cards.name: Vanillish
cards.flavorText: Snowy mountains are this Pokémon's habitat. During an ancient ice age, they moved to southern areas.

cards.name: Vanilluxe
cards.flavorText: Swallowing large amounts of water, they make snow clouds inside their bodies and attack their foes with violent blizzards.

cards.name: Blitzle
cards.flavorText: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use their flashing manes to communicate with one another.

cards.name: Zebstrika
cards.flavorText: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.

cards.name: Joltik
cards.flavorText: Joltik that live in cities have learned a technique for sucking electricity from the outlets in houses.

cards.name: Galvantula
cards.flavorText: When attacked, they create an electric barrier by spitting out many electrically charged threads.

cards.name: Stunfisk
cards.flavorText: Its skin is very hard, so it is unhurt even if stepped on by sumo wrestlers. It smiles when transmitting electricity.

cards.name: Woobat
cards.flavorText: Its habitat is dark forests and caves. It emits ultrasonic waves from its nose to learn about its surroundings.

cards.name: Swoobat
cards.flavorText: It emits sound waves of various frequencies from its nose, including some powerful enough to destroy rocks.

cards.name: Sigilyph
cards.flavorText: They never vary the route they fly, because their memories of guarding an ancient city remain steadfast.

cards.name: Yamask
cards.flavorText: Each of them carries a mask that used to be its face when it was human. Sometimes they look at it and cry.

cards.name: Cofagrigus
cards.flavorText: It has been said that they swallow those who get too close and turn them into mummies. They like to eat gold nuggets.

cards.name: Gothita
cards.flavorText: Their ribbonlike feelers increase their psychic power. They are always staring at something.

cards.name: Gothorita
cards.flavorText: They use hypnosis to control people and Pokémon. Tales of Gothorita leading people astray are told in every corner.

cards.name: Gothitelle
cards.flavorText: Starry skies thousands of light-years away are visible in the space distorted by their intense psychic power.

cards.name: Frillish
cards.flavorText: With its thin, veil-like arms wrapped around the body of its opponent, it sinks to the ocean floor.

ability.name: Oceanic Curse
ability.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent can't play any Item cards or Pokémon Tool cards from their hand.

cards.name: Roggenrola
cards.flavorText: Its ear is hexagonal in shape. Compressed underground, its body is as hard as steel.

cards.name: Boldore
cards.flavorText: When it overflows with power, the orange crystal on its body glows. It looks for underground water in caves.

cards.name: Gigalith
cards.flavorText: Compressing the energy from its internal core lets it fire off an attack capable of blowing away a mountain.

cards.name: Sawk
cards.flavorText: The sound of Sawk punching boulders and trees can be heard all the way from the mountains where they train.

cards.name: Archen
cards.flavorText: Said to be an ancestor of bird Pokémon, they were unable to fly and moved about by hopping from one branch to another.

cards.name: Archeops
cards.flavorText: They are intelligent and will cooperate to catch prey. From the ground, they use a running start to take flight.

cards.name: Mienfoo
cards.flavorText: In fights, they dominate with onslaughts of flowing, continuous attacks. With their sharp claws, they cut enemies.

cards.name: Mienshao
cards.flavorText: It wields the fur on its arms like a whip. Its arm attacks come with such rapidity that they cannot even be seen.

cards.name: Terrakion
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon came to the defense of Pokémon that had lost their homes in a war among humans.

cards.name: Purrloin
cards.flavorText: They steal from people for fun, but their victims can't help but forgive them. Their deceptively cute act is perfect.

cards.name: Liepard
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon vanish and appear unexpectedly. Many Trainers are drawn to their beautiful form and fur.

cards.name: Scraggy
cards.flavorText: Its skin has a rubbery elasticity, so it can reduce damage by defensively pulling its skin up to its neck.

cards.name: Scrafty
cards.flavorText: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.

cards.name: Trubbish
cards.flavorText: Inhaling the gas they belch will make you sleep for a week. They prefer unsanitary places.

cards.name: Garbodor
cards.flavorText: It clenches opponents with its left arm and finishes them off with foul-smelling poison gas belched from its mouth.

cards.name: Zorua
cards.flavorText: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.

cards.name: Zoroark
cards.flavorText: Bonds between these Pokémon are very strong. It protects the safety of its pack by tricking its opponents.

cards.name: Vullaby
cards.flavorText: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.

cards.name: Mandibuzz
cards.flavorText: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.

cards.name: Deino
cards.flavorText: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.

cards.name: Zweilous
cards.flavorText: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.

ability.name: Greedy Eater
ability.text: If your opponent's Basic Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack used by this Pokémon, take 1 more Prize card.

cards.name: Ferroseed
cards.flavorText: When threatened, it attacks by shooting a barrage of spikes, which gives it a chance to escape by rolling away.

cards.name: Ferrothorn
cards.flavorText: It fights by swinging around its three spiky feelers. A hit from these steel spikes can reduce a boulder to rubble.

cards.name: Durant
cards.flavorText: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.

cards.name: Druddigon
cards.flavorText: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.

cards.name: Patrat
cards.flavorText: Using food stored in cheek pouches, they can keep watch for days. They use their tails to communicate with others.

cards.name: Watchog
cards.flavorText: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

cards.name: Lillipup
cards.flavorText: It faces strong opponents with great courage. But, when at a disadvantage in a fight, this intelligent Pokémon flees.

cards.name: Herdier
cards.flavorText: It has black, cape-like fur that is very hard and decreases the amount of damage it receives.

cards.name: Stoutland
cards.flavorText: It rescues people stranded by blizzards in the mountains. Its shaggy fur shields it from the cold.

ability.name: Bouffer
ability.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Tornadus
cards.flavorText: The lower half of its body is wrapped in a cloud of energy. It zooms through the sky at 200 mph.

cards.name: Sewaddle
cards.flavorText: Leavanny dress it in clothes they made for it when it hatched. It hides its head in its hood while it is sleeping.

cards.flavorText: They steal from people for fun, but their victims can't help but forgive them. Their deceptively cute act is perfect.

cards.name: Liepard
cards.flavorText: These Pokémon vanish and appear unexpectedly. Many Trainers are drawn to their beautiful form and fur.

cards.name: Scraggy
cards.flavorText: Its skin has a rubbery elasticity, so it can reduce damage by defensively pulling its skin up to its neck.

cards.name: Scrafty
cards.flavorText: Groups of them beat up anything that enters their territory. Each can spit acidic liquid from its mouth.

cards.name: Trubbish
cards.flavorText: Inhaling the gas they belch will make you sleep for a week. They prefer unsanitary places.

cards.name: Garbodor
cards.flavorText: It clenches opponents with its left arm and finishes them off with foul-smelling poison gas belched from its mouth.

cards.name: Zorua
cards.flavorText: It changes into the forms of others to surprise them. Apparently, it often transforms into a silent child.

cards.name: Zoroark
cards.flavorText: Bonds between these Pokémon are very strong. It protects the safety of its pack by tricking its opponents.

cards.name: Vullaby
cards.flavorText: Its wings are too tiny to allow it to fly. As the time approaches for it to evolve, it discards the bones it was wearing.

cards.name: Mandibuzz
cards.flavorText: It makes a nest out of bones it finds. It grabs weakened prey in its talons and hauls it to its nest of bones.

cards.name: Deino
cards.flavorText: It tends to bite everything, and it is not a picky eater. Approaching it carelessly is dangerous.

cards.name: Zweilous
cards.flavorText: After it has eaten up all the food in its territory, it moves to another area. Its two heads do not get along.

cards.name: Ferroseed
cards.flavorText: When threatened, it attacks by shooting a barrage of spikes, which gives it a chance to escape by rolling away.

cards.name: Ferrothorn
cards.flavorText: It fights by swinging around its three spiky feelers. A hit from these steel spikes can reduce a boulder to rubble.

cards.name: Durant
cards.flavorText: They attack in groups, covering themselves in steel armor to protect themselves from Heatmor.

cards.name: Druddigon
cards.flavorText: It warms its body by absorbing sunlight with its wings. When its body temperature falls, it can no longer move.

cards.name: Patrat
cards.flavorText: Using food stored in cheek pouches, they can keep watch for days. They use their tails to communicate with others.

cards.name: Watchog
cards.flavorText: When they see an enemy, their tails stand high, and they spit the seeds of berries stored in their cheek pouches.

cards.name: Lillipup
cards.flavorText: It faces strong opponents with great courage. But, when at a disadvantage in a fight, this intelligent Pokémon flees.

cards.name: Herdier
cards.flavorText: It has black, cape-like fur that is very hard and decreases the amount of damage it receives.

cards.name: Stoutland
cards.flavorText: It rescues people stranded by blizzards in the mountains. Its shaggy fur shields it from the cold.

ability.name: Oceanic Curse
ability.text: As long as this Pokémon is in the Active Spot, your opponent can't play any Item cards or Pokémon Tool cards from their hand.

ability.name: Greedy Eater
ability.text: If your opponent's Basic Pokémon is Knocked Out by damage from an attack used by this Pokémon, take 1 more Prize card.

ability.name: Bouffer
ability.text: This Pokémon takes 30 less damage from attacks (after applying Weakness and Resistance).

cards.name: Victini
cards.flavorText: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

ability.text: Once during your turn, when you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon, you may use this Ability. Search your deck for a Shedinja and put it onto your Bench. Then, shuffle your deck.

ability.name: Intimidating Fang

ability.name: Explosiveness
ability.text: If this Pokémon is in your hand when you are setting up to play, you may put it face down in the Active Spot.

ability.name: Heave-Ho Catcher
ability.text: Once during your turn, when you play this Pokémon from your hand to evolve 1 of your Pokémon, you may use this Ability. Switch in 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon to the Active Spot.

ability.name: Lunar Cycle
ability.text: Once during your turn, if you have Solrock in play, you may discard a Basic Fighting Energy card from your hand in order to use this Ability. Draw 3 cards. You can't use more than 1 Lunar Cycle Ability each turn.

ability.name: Haphazard Hammer

ability.name: Lustrous Assist
ability.text: Once during your turn, when your Mega Latias ex moves from your Bench to the Active Spot, you may use this Ability. Move any amount of Energy from your Benched Pokémon to your Active Pokémon.
